meta.title: Advanced English Grammar Test (C1-C2) - Movies, Series, and Anime
meta.description: A comprehensive test covering English Participle Clauses themed around Movies, Series, and Anime, combining at least two advanced concepts per question.
meta.info: This test includes 30 questions focusing on combined C1-C2 level grammar structures, primarily featuring Participle Clauses paired with other complex topics like inversion, subjunctive mood, conditionals, and more.
meta.author: Qwen3.7

data.hint: Choose the correct structures to complete the sentence.
data.question: Having watched the entire series in one sitting, rarely _____ such a compelling plot twist.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause ('Having watched') with negative adverbial inversion. 'Rarely' at the beginning of the main clause triggers subject-auxiliary inversion ('have I witnessed').
explanation.concept: Perfect participle followed by negative adverbial inversion
explanation.formula: Having + past participle, rarely + auxiliary + subject + past participle
examples: Having seen the show, never have I been so moved.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a present participle clause ('Demanding') with the mandative subjunctive. After 'demanding that', the verb must be in the base form ('cut'), and 'insisted it be' requires the base form 'be' for the subjunctive mood.
explanation.concept: Present participle introducing a mandative subjunctive clause
explanation.formula: Demanding that + subject + base verb, having + past participle, insisted + subject + base verb
examples: Demanding that the band rehearse, the manager, having arrived early, insisted it be perfect.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Had the studio not intervened, the anime, having been adapted faithfully, _____ a commercial failure.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect passive participle clause ('having been adapted') with a third conditional inversion ('Had the studio not intervened'), requiring 'would have been' in the main clause.
explanation.concept: Perfect passive participle embedded in a third conditional
explanation.formula: Had + subject + not + past participle, noun, having been + past participle, would have + past participle
examples: Had they not helped, the project, having been delayed, would have failed.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines an it-cleft sentence with a perfect participle clause. 'It was' is required for singular emphasis. 'Having captured' is the correct perfect participle form. The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the singular 'cinematographer', requiring 'deserves'.
explanation.concept: Perfect participle within a cleft sentence structure
explanation.formula: It + was + singular noun, having + past participle, who + singular verb
examples: It was the artist, having painted the mural, who deserves the award.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: Believed to have been inspired by a true story, the film, recently discovered, _____ by critics.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect passive participle clause ('Believed to have been inspired') with a present continuous passive structure ('is currently being analyzed') in the main clause.
explanation.concept: Perfect passive participle followed by present continuous passive
explanation.formula: Believed to have been + past participle, noun, is/are + currently + being + past participle
examples: Thought to have been lost, the artifact is being examined.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause ('having been filming') with the future perfect continuous tense ('will have been performing') to emphasize duration up to a future point.
explanation.concept: Perfect participle indicating duration leading to future perfect continuous
explanation.formula: By + future time, having been + verb-ing, subject + will have been + verb-ing
examples: By 2025, having been working here for ten years, she will have been managing the team.

data.hint: Choose the correct modal verb to complete the sentence.
data.question: Having heard the raw audio, the sound engineer _____ impressed by the actor's exceptional range.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause ('Having heard') with a modal verb of deduction about the past ('must have been').
explanation.topic: Participle Clauses + Modal Verbs of Deduction
explanation.concept: Perfect participle leading to a past logical deduction
explanation.formula: Having + past participle, subject + must have + been + adjective
examples: Having seen the results, he must have been relieved.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a non-defining relative clause with a perfect participle clause. 'Film' is the subject of the active action of receiving acclaim, requiring the active perfect participle 'having received', not the passive 'having been received'.
explanation.concept: Perfect participle within relative clauses
explanation.formula: Noun, whose + noun, having + past participle + object, + main verb
examples: The author, whose book, having sold millions, is a bestseller.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Having decided _____ a career in animation, the artist avoided _____ her previous failures.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause ('Having decided') with specific verb patterns. 'Decide' takes a to-infinitive ('to pursue'), and 'avoid' takes a gerund ('mentioning').
explanation.concept: Perfect participle followed by specific verb patterns
explanation.formula: Having decided + to-infinitive, subject + avoided + gerund
examples: Having chosen to leave, she avoided discussing it.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines an elliptical adverbial clause with a perfect passive participle clause. 'Although considered' is the correct passive ellipsis (Although it is considered).
explanation.concept: Elliptical passive constructions with participle clauses
explanation.formula: Although + past participle, noun, having been + past participle, + verb
examples: Although praised by critics, the film, having been poorly marketed, failed.

data.hint: Choose the correct discourse marker to complete the sentence.
data.question: Having faced numerous production delays, the series, _____, managed to secure a renewal.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause ('Having faced') with a contrastive discourse marker ('nevertheless') to show opposition to the expected outcome.
explanation.concept: Perfect participle with contrastive discourse markers
explanation.formula: Having + past participle + object, subject, nevertheless, + verb
examples: Having lost funding, the project, nevertheless, continued.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a double comparative structure with a perfect participle clause. 'Better' is already comparative, so 'more' is incorrect.
explanation.concept: Double comparatives followed by perfect participle clauses
explanation.formula: The + comparative + subject + verb, the + comparative + subject + verb, having + past participle
examples: The harder he trained, the faster he ran, having focused on his technique.

data.hint: Choose the correct structures to complete the sentence.
data.question: What astonished the critics, _____ the premiere, was the sheer originality of the screenplay.

explanation.text: This combines a noun clause acting as the subject ('What astonished the critics') with a perfect active participle clause ('having attended') modifying 'the critics'.
explanation.concept: Perfect participle modifying the subject of a noun clause
explanation.formula: What + verb + object, having + past participle + object, was + noun phrase
examples: What surprised the guests, having arrived early, was the decoration.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause ('having realized') with a verb pattern. 'Suggest' must be followed by a gerund ('having'), not a to-infinitive.
explanation.concept: Perfect participle following a gerund verb pattern
explanation.formula: Subject + suggested + having + object + past participle, having + past participle
examples: He suggested going out, having finished his work.

data.hint: Choose the correct structures to complete the sentence.
data.question: Having run out of ideas, the showrunner decided to _____ the release date until further notice.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause ('Having run out') with a separable phrasal verb ('put off', meaning to postpone).
explanation.concept: Perfect participle followed by phrasal verb usage
explanation.formula: Having run out of + noun, subject + decided to + phrasal verb + object
examples: Having run out of time, we decided to call off the meeting.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect passive participle clause ('Having been oblivious') with an adjective + preposition collocation. 'Oblivious' is followed by 'to', not 'for'.
explanation.concept: Perfect participle with specific adjective-preposition collocations
explanation.formula: Having been + adjective + to + noun, subject + verb
examples: Having been accustomed to the noise, he slept soundly.

data.hint: Choose the correct article to complete the sentence.
data.question: Having composed _____ unique melody for the soundtrack, the musician was widely praised by his peers.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause ('Having composed') with article usage. 'Unique' starts with a consonant sound (/j/), so it correctly takes the indefinite article 'a'.
explanation.concept: Perfect participle followed by indefinite article before a consonant sound
explanation.formula: Having + past participle + a + word starting with /j/ sound
examples: Having built a unique structure, the architect won an award.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause ('Having reviewed') with a quantifier in a relative clause. 'Scripts' is countable and plural, requiring 'few of which', not 'little of which'.
explanation.concept: Perfect participle followed by countable quantifiers in relative clauses
explanation.formula: Having reviewed + plural countable noun, few of which + plural verb
examples: Having read the books, few of which were interesting, he stopped.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to ensure subject-verb agreement.
data.question: The number of episodes, having been reduced by the network, _____ decreased, while a number of plotlines _____ unresolved.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect passive participle clause ('having been reduced') with subject-verb agreement rules. 'The number of' takes a singular verb ('has'), while 'a number of' takes a plural verb ('remain').
explanation.concept: Perfect participle interrupting 'the number of' vs. 'a number of'
explanation.formula: The number of + noun, having been + past participle, has + verb; a number of + noun + plural verb
examples: The number of errors, having been noted, has dropped, while a number of issues remain.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: invested more in CGI, the film,

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause ('having relied') with 'If only' for past regret, which requires the past perfect ('had invested').
explanation.concept: Perfect participle embedded in a past regret structure
explanation.formula: If only + subject + had + past participle, having + past participle, subject + would have + past participle
examples: If only I had studied, having understood the material, I would have passed.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: Having wasted enough time on minor details, it is high time the producers _____ the film.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause ('Having wasted') with the 'it's high time' structure, which requires the past subjunctive ('released') to indicate present urgency.
explanation.concept: Perfect participle leading to 'it's high time' + past simple
explanation.formula: Having + past participle + object, it is high time + subject + past simple
examples: Having waited long enough, it is high time we left.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: the character deeply, behaves as though

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause ('having studied') with 'as though' + past subjunctive ('composed') to describe an unreal or hypothetical present situation.
explanation.topic: Participle Clauses + As Though / As If
explanation.concept: Perfect participle followed by unreal comparison
explanation.formula: Noun, having + past participle + object, behaves as though + subject + past simple
examples: The actor, having memorized the lines, acts as though he wrote the script.

data.hint: Choose the correct structures to complete the inverted sentence.
data.question: So captivating was the performance, _____ for months, that the audience gave a standing ovation.

explanation.text: This combines 'so + adjective' inversion ('So captivating was') with a perfect passive participle clause ('having been rehearsed') for emphasis.
explanation.concept: Perfect passive participle within an inverted emphatic structure
explanation.formula: So + adjective + be + subject, having been + past participle, that + clause
examples: So intense was the storm, having been predicted, that roads closed.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause ('having been rushed') with third conditional inversion. The correct inversion for a past unreal condition is 'Had + subject + not + past participle'.
explanation.concept: Perfect participle embedded in a third conditional inversion
explanation.formula: Had + subject + not + past participle, having + past participle, subject + would have + past participle
examples: Had they not missed the train, having left late, they would have arrived on time.

data.hint: Choose the correct structures to complete the sentence.
data.question: Not only did the writer create the universe, but having designed the characters as well, she _____ directed the pilot.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause ('having designed') with the correlative conjunction 'not only... but also' and inversion.
explanation.topic: Participle Clauses + Not Only ... But Also
explanation.concept: Perfect participle within a 'not only... but also' structure
explanation.formula: Not only + auxiliary + subject + verb, but having + past participle + object, subject + also + verb
examples: Not only did she design the dress, but having sewn it, she also modeled it.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: the rights to his own anime.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause ('having signed') with negative adverbial inversion. 'Little' at the beginning of a clause requires subject-auxiliary inversion ('did the creator know').
explanation.topic: Participle Clauses + Little Did He Know
explanation.concept: Perfect participle interrupting negative adverbial inversion
explanation.formula: Little + auxiliary + subject + base verb, having + past participle, that + clause
examples: Little did he know, having agreed to the terms, that he would regret it.

data.hint: Choose the correct structures to complete the sentence.
data.question: Under no circumstances should the unreleased episode, _____ leaked online, be distributed further.

explanation.text: This combines negative adverbial inversion ('Under no circumstances should') with a perfect passive participle clause ('having been leaked').
explanation.concept: Perfect passive participle within negative inversion
explanation.formula: Under no circumstances + auxiliary + subject + verb, having been + past participle, + main verb
examples: Under no circumstances should the document, having been classified, be shared.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause ('having never used') with first conditional inversion. 'Should' must be followed by the base form of the verb ('need'), not the gerund.
explanation.concept: Perfect participle following conditional inversion
explanation.formula: Should + subject + base verb, having + past participle, imperative
examples: Should you require help, having never tried this, please ask.

data.hint: Choose the correct structures to complete the sentence.
data.question: Were I to choose a favorite scene, _____ the series multiple times, it would be the final battle.

explanation.text: This combines second conditional inversion ('Were I to choose') with a perfect active participle clause ('having watched').
explanation.concept: Perfect participle embedded in second conditional inversion
explanation.formula: Were + subject + to + base verb, having + past participle, subject + would + base verb
examples: Were I to pick one, having seen them all, it would be the red one.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: of the manga for years, she now

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause ('Having been') with mixed tenses. The main clause is in the present ('now'), so the third-person singular subject 'she' requires the present simple verb 'watches'.
explanation.concept: Perfect participle indicating past duration leading to a present simple main clause
explanation.formula: Having been + noun + for + time, subject + present simple verb
examples: Having lived here for years, he now knows the city well.
